story: Three weeks ago, Leora Venn left Covehollow with a small suitcase and said she would return the Legion hall keys by post. The keys have not arrived, although she paid her rent before leaving and took her purse and coat. Some neighbours think she needed a rest, while others have begun to ask where she went.

pages.title: Welcome to the Reading Room
pages.content:
WELCOME TO THE READING ROOM

The Covehollow Reading Room is open Tuesdays and Thursdays from two o'clock until five, and on Saturday mornings following chapel prayers. Borrowers may take two volumes for up to three weeks. Please handle our books with clean hands and return them promptly so your neighbours may enjoy them.

We are currently in need of clean paperback donations in good repair, especially devotional readings, gardening guides, and gentle travel memoirs. Kindly leave any parcels with Tamsin Rooke at the main desk rather than on the porch step.

> Local Collections readingroom.cv/collections
> Things We Are Looking For readingroom.cv/looking

pages.title: Local Collections
pages.content:
LOCAL COLLECTIONS

Our small archive preserves the paper records of Covehollow for study and remembrance. Visitors are welcome to consult our binders during regular desk hours.

Holdings currently include:
- Photographic prints of the government pier reconstruction, 1912-1914.
- The day ledger from the old lower harbour forge, recording shoeing and boat irons from 1891 onward.
- Parish auxiliary minutes and floral committee rosters.

Our archive has a local programme copied out after the Ostend Convention in 1927.

We also preserve the handwritten scorecards from the autumn card socials at the hall:
1st: M. Cleary and partner
2nd: A. Ashworth and partner
3rd: P. Cloutier and partner

May our past labours remind us of Providence's quiet care.

pages.title: Things We Are Looking For
pages.content:
THINGS WE ARE LOOKING FOR

To ensure our village history remains whole for the generations to follow, the reading room welcomes gifts of paper ephemera.

We are presently seeking:
- Printed notices and price sheets from the early years of the fishermen's co-op.
- Photographs of the old harbour forge taken before its cedar roof was replaced in 1954.
- Spare copies of church festival programmes prior to 1965.

The reading room keeps a scrapbook of village clippings about Kestrel 9 in 1979.

If you have kept any of these items in your attic or drawers, please speak with Tamsin Rooke. Even a brief loan for copying is deeply appreciated.

pages.title: Village Office
pages.content:
VILLAGE OFFICE

Welcome to the official village office page for Covehollow. Orin Bell, council clerk, is present weekdays from half past eight in the morning until quarter past noon, and on Thursday afternoons for harbour dues.

Outside of posted office hours, residents are asked to drop written messages into the tin slot beside the front door. We hold all neighbours in our thoughts and thank you for your charity and patience while letters are attended to in proper order.

> Council Minutes council.cv/minutes
> Road Notices council.cv/roads

pages.title: Council Minutes
pages.content:
COUNCIL MINUTES

Minutes of the regular meeting held on the second Tuesday of the month.

Members present: J. Calder, M. Teague, O. Bell (clerk). Opening prayer offered by Mr Calder.

1. Pier Railing. Approval was granted to purchase fir timber and galvanized brackets to repair the handrail near the eastern slipway. The office retained a copy of the Osaka specification from 1969 with its records of approved supplies.

2. Winter Grading. A decision regarding the hiring of private grader equipment for the road past the churchyard was deferred until November. The clerk will inquire about salt stockpiles.

Meeting closed with a collection for parish welfare.

pages.title: Road Notices
pages.content:
ROAD NOTICES

Autumn ruts and gravel washouts have been noted along the parish routes following the hard rain on Michaelmas.

The council requests that washouts on the west road past the gravel pit be reported to the office without delay. Drivers of coal carts and heavy wagons should exercise Christian forbearance and keep to the crown of the roadway until crushed stone can be laid.

Please notify Orin Bell of any blocked stone culverts before frost sets into the ditches.

pages.title: Co-op Noticeboard
pages.content:
COVEHOLLOW FISH CO-OPERATIVE

Welcome to the landing, packing, and supplies office at the south pier. We serve sixty-four shareholding boats and their families.

Ice must be requested eight hours before your vessel leaves moorings. Please ring the scalehouse on line four between seven and four. May God grant smooth water to all our crews this week.

Members are reminded that the tea urn in the packing shed is for common comfort and should be rinsed after each shift.

> Landing Times coop.cv/landings
> Supplies and Repairs coop.cv/supplies

pages.title: Landing Times
pages.content:
LANDING TIMES AND PIER USE

The co-operative scales open at five in the morning and close at half past six in the evening from Monday through Saturday. No scales are manned on the Lord's Day.

Boats expecting to tie up outside these hours must telephone the wharfmaster or leave word at the office before four in the afternoon. Late arrivals without prior word cause needless worry to those waiting on the road.

We ask that decks be swilled down promptly so salt and gurry do not sit on the lower steps. Prayers are offered each morning at first weighing for those out beyond the heads.

> Co-op Noticeboard coop.cv
> Supplies and Repairs coop.cv/supplies

pages.title: Supplies and Repairs
pages.content:
SUPPLIES AND REPAIRS

The supply room carries heavy oiled wool, cotton work gloves, yellow twine, and stiff manila line in standard hanks. Buckets and salt cakes are kept under the shed roof.

For chain splicing, link welding, or small metal repairs on winches and gaffs, we recommend the shop beside the old forge on Back Lane. Kindly settle accounts with them directly, as the co-op ledger does not carry outside smithing.

Perrin Moss is on duty in the stores from eight until dinner time. Let us deal with one another in patience and fair charity.

> Co-op Noticeboard coop.cv
> Landing Times coop.cv/landings

pages.title: Village Noticeboard
pages.content:
COVEHOLLOW RESIDENT NOTICEBOARD

Welcome to our electronic message board for Covehollow. This board is provided so neighbours may confer in Christian charity, share small domestic news, and offer help to those who stand in need.

Please remember to be gentle in your enquiries. Let us sign our names where possible and keep every neighbour's privacy in our prayers, as our parish teaches.

Active discussions this week:

> Has Anyone Heard from Leora? noticeboard.cv/forum/t/114
> Getting to the Gravel Pit noticeboard.cv/forum/t/119

May peace rest upon your household.

pages.title: Has Anyone Heard from Leora?
pages.content:
Thread: Has Anyone Heard from Leora?

[greta_at_home] Please remember our Christian forbearance in this thread. Leora paid her lodging through Michaelmas and took her good brown coat. There is no cause for alarm.
[halltable] She told me at the hall door three weeks back that she would post the hall pantry keys from town once she arrived, but the post has brought nothing yet. We pray she is well rested.
[sundaytea] She left two jars of crab-apple jelly on the church vestry shelf with a slip of paper for the fete. Third prize (marrow): A. Ashworth was written on the back of the envelope, from last autumn's list.
[shelfkeeper] She returned her three library volumes very neatly. She said she was listening for an old broadcast. My gran said the Ostend Convention in 1927 meant she could finally listen to a little station she liked.
[sheeteditor] My mother saved the supper dishes for later so she could hear the news of Kestrel 1 in 1966.
[officeorin] If the keys do not come by Saturday we can cut a duplicate from the parish ring. There is no need to trouble the county constable when someone has merely gone on a visit.

pages.title: Getting to the Gravel Pit
pages.content:
Thread: Getting to the Gravel Pit

[ropeandice] Has anyone taken a cart up the old west track toward the pit this month? The parish ditch has overflowed by the lower turn.
[greta_at_home] Most use the harbour road now for all haulage. Does anyone remember the co-op putting up a notice for the Meridian Line in 1952?
[sheeteditor] We walked that road every Sunday before the wharf was widened. My uncle said half the harbour wanted to talk about the Glasgow match in 1944.
[halltable] It is very overgrown with brambles now. Only the children go up to look for elderberries, though Leora used to walk that way toward the ridge in the evenings. We must pray for dry weather so the lower culvert drains properly.

pages.title: This Month's Sheet
pages.content:
THE COVEHOLLOW SHEET - OCTOBER ISSUE

Welcome to the web edition of our village newsletter, prepared monthly through the generosity of our subscribers.

PARISH AND COMMUNITY NOTICES

St. Jude-in-the-Cove will take up a special second collection this Lord's Day for the diocesan winter fuel fund. Sisterly remembrances are asked for all travelling parishioners.

The co-op counter opens at six each morning for ice, fuel and salt barrels, closing promptly at four for evening prayers.

The Legion autumn fish supper is fixed for Thursday the twenty-second. Hall volunteers are kindly asked to assist with table settings from three o'clock onward.

> A Harbour in Pictures sheet.cv/history/harbour
> The Old Forge sheet.cv/history/forge

pages.title: A Harbour in Pictures
pages.content:
A HARBOUR IN PICTURES

From our archive of glass slides preserved through the decades, we present views of Covehollow's water gate.

In the earliest plates, the stone pier terminates thirty feet short of its present reach. Fishermen hauled dories over round logs before the steam winch was installed by general subscription.

The Sheet's earliest editor recorded that several villagers gathered to hear about the Glasgow match in 1944.

Later photographs from the nineteen-sixties show the first clapboard shed built beside the slips by our co-op elders. Three generations of men stand upon the salt-wharf in Sunday woollens, their hands folded in quiet thankfulness for a prosperous season.

May their industry remain an example to us all.

pages.title: The Old Forge
pages.content:
THE OLD FORGE

Behind the net-drying racks stands the stone gable of the old smithy, where Master Cleary once worked iron for our fathers and grandfathers.

Fishers carried their broken cod-hooks, boom-bands and rudder-hinges up from the slips to be laid upon the anvil. The hearth fire was banked only on the Sabbath, and neighbours often lingered at the doorway to share quiet conversation out of the salt wind.

The Meridian Line in 1952 brought enough interest at the harbour that the Sheet printed a small map.

For Kestrel 9 in 1979, neighbours gathered at the hall and shared tea after the landing.

Though the forge cold-chisel has rested these twenty years, the masonry stands firm, reminding us of quiet duty well rendered.

pages.title: Welcome and Worship
pages.content:
WELCOME AND WORSHIP

Covehollow Community Church welcomes all neighbours, seasonal visitors, and travellers who come through our harbour. 

Morning Prayer is observed every Sunday at 10:00 a.m., followed by the general service at 10:30 a.m. We invite all in attendance to remain in the vestry afterwards for a cup of hot tea and fellowship. Evensong is held on the first Wednesday of each month at 6:30 p.m.

We continue to remember those who are travelling afar or resting away from home. Enquiries regarding pastoral visits, flowers, or transport may be left with Mrs. Harrow.

> Church Calendar church.cv/calendar
> Autumn Fete Raffle church.cv/fete-prizes

pages.title: Church Calendar
pages.content:
CHURCH CALENDAR

NOVEMBER AND DECEMBER

Sunday, 22 November: Regular morning worship. We continue our prayer list for quiet journeys and absent friends.

Wednesday, 25 November: Midweek vestry cleaning and flower arranging, 2:00 p.m.

Sunday, 29 November: Beginning of our Advent collection of warm socks and woollen mittens for the harbour mission. A basket is placed near the font.

Thursday, 3 December: First rehearsal for the carol service in the main hall at 7:00 p.m. All voices are welcome.

At the Sunday service after Kestrel 1 in 1966, we gave thanks for the traveller's safe return.

May peace and charity guide our steps through the cold season.

pages.title: Autumn Fete Raffle
pages.content:
AUTUMN FETE RAFFLE

The committee wishes to thank everyone who purchased tickets in support of the roof repair fund. The winning ticket numbers and prizes are listed below:

Ticket 014: M. Dace — Basket of crab apples
Ticket 047: P. Moss — Tin of butter biscuits
Ticket 082: A. Ashworth — tea towel
Ticket 119: T. Rooke — Jar of plum preserves
Ticket 143: Unclaimed — Knitted wool scarf

Mr. Ashworth's ticket gave a village address, though neighbours do not recall meeting him during the sale. He may collect the linen from the vestry cupboard after Sunday tea.

After the Lighthouse Act in 1936, our congregation sent a letter of thanks to the keepers who tended the light.

pages.title: At the Hall
pages.content:
COVEHOLLOW ROYAL CANADIAN LEGION BRANCH HALL

Welcome to our hall page. We remain dedicated to quiet service, good fellowship, and providing a warm gathering place for all neighbours along the shore.

Our monthly Saturday supper will take place on the third weekend of the month, God willing. Cold ham, turnip mash, brown bread, and tea will be served at five o'clock. A donation basket will sit beside the door in aid of parish charity.

For hall availability and private rentals, please consult our bookings notice or speak directly with Mrs. Ailsa Fenwick. We ask your forbearance as some regular duties are being shared amongst the committee at present.

> Hall Bookings legion.cv/bookings
> Tuesday Quiz Results legion.cv/quiz-results

pages.title: Tuesday Quiz Results
pages.content:
TUESDAY NIGHT TRIVIA RESULTS

Thank you to the seven teams who sat for our weekly Bible and maritime trivia night. Fellowship was enjoyed by all, and five dollars and twenty cents was gathered for the flower fund.

Final standings:
1. The Harbour Lights — 24 points
2. Saint Jude's Circle — 21 points
3. The Co-op Slip — 19 points
4. A. Ashworth — 12 points
5. South Head Table — 10 points

A note from the scorer's table: Mr. or Miss A. Ashworth played alone in the back row and marked their paper as a resident of Covehollow. None of the committee recall meeting them before Tuesday, but we pray they found our hall hospitable and will return next week.

pages.title: Hall Bookings
pages.content:
HALL BOOKINGS AND KEYS

The hall is open for prayer circles, carpet bowling, and family gatherings. Rental fees remain modest to assist the community.

Important notice regarding entry: We kindly ask all groups and organisers to arrange key collection well in advance with Ailsa Fenwick. Miss Leora Venn is away from the village on rest and has not yet returned the committee key ring by parcel post as expected. 

Until the post brings the spare set from her travels, we must open and lock the front vestibule by hand. Please give two days' notice before any evening use so someone may walk down with the padlock bar.

traffic.subject: Altar guild linens and Legion tea
traffic.body: Good evening Ailsa. We have washed the small linen cloths for St. Jude's tide. When you unlock the hall tomorrow for the prayer group tea, could you let me know if the back drawer in the scullery has the extra cups? We pray Leora is finding quiet wherever she is resting, but we did hope the parcel with the keys might arrive on today's post.

traffic.subject: Re: Altar guild linens and Legion tea
traffic.body: Celia, no parcel on the four o'clock van. Duncan had to let me in with the heavy brass latchkey from the forge end of the cellar. The scullery has forty cups ready. We remember Leora in our evening intercessions here at home. She was always so punctual with the hall logs.

traffic.subject: Minutes of the harbour bench committee
traffic.body: Tamsin, have you the minutes from November 1982 regarding the stone bench down by the pier? Mr. Cloutier says it was placed by subscription, but the council roll has no receipt for the mortar. Hope your knees are easier in the damp tonight.

traffic.subject: Re: Minutes of the harbour bench committee
traffic.body: Orin, the pier file is right here on the shelf beside the parish registers. It was indeed private subscription—mostly widows' pence. While looking, I noticed on the old roll of subscribers the name 'A. Ashworth' down for two shillings. It is curious, because nobody in the room has ever known an A. Ashworth in the cove.

traffic.subject: Winter salt order notice
traffic.body: Merrin, please put a short paragraph in the weekly sheet: salt bags will be stacked inside the shed door, not out on the wharf deck, starting Michaelmas. People must sign the ledger. Has Leora's niece written from Truro at all, do you know? Her oil account here is settled, but her winter kerosene voucher sits on my spike.

traffic.subject: Re: Winter salt order notice
traffic.body: I will set the notice in eight-point type near the tide table. No one has heard from any family in Truro, Perrin. Celia says we should assume she is taking a fortnight's retreat for her lungs, but three weeks is long for a woman who never missed Sunday matins.

traffic.subject: Board post about the hall booking
traffic.body: Ailsa, someone posted an anonymous query on the dial-in board asking who has the master key for the whist tournament. I hid the message for now because people began asking whether Leora had left the province entirely. I prefer to keep the board peaceful and avoid idle talk.

traffic.subject: Re: Board post about the hall booking
traffic.body: Thank you, Greta. That was prudent. She paid her room rent to Mrs. Gedge right to the end of next month, and took only her small valise and the wool coat. The Lord will see her footsteps guided. Still, the lock on the back door ought not to be forced if she simply forgot to drop the envelope in the postbox before boarding the coach.

traffic.subject: Re: Minutes of the harbour bench committee
traffic.body: A. Ashworth is also entered on the ratepayer list for the common pump in 1954, though no house lot is attached. Father used to say it was an error copied forward by lazy clerks. Pray do not spend your lamps on it; check the pier stonework receipt when you have a free half-hour.

traffic.subject: Collect for next Sunday
traffic.body: Merrin, could you print the Collect for St. Luke's Day on the front page? Especially the part about wholesome medicines of doctrine. We had three women in the vestry this afternoon asking if anyone had checked Leora's garden. The cabbages are rotting on the stem, which is unlike her.

traffic.subject: Re: Collect for next Sunday
traffic.body: I will include it, Celia. Perhaps Perrin or young Ronald could cut the cabbages and bring them to the parish poor-box before frost gets them? It seems a pity to waste God's earth-gifts while we wait for her card.

traffic.subject: Parish roll curiosity
traffic.body: Celia dear, while hunting out the 1930s charity lists for Orin, I saw that name again: A. Ashworth. Signed for five pounds of meal during the lean winter of 1941. Nobody ever saw who collected the bag. Has the rector ever found that name in the baptismal or burial volumes?

traffic.subject: Re: Parish roll curiosity
traffic.body: Never, Tamsin. I have indexed back to 1888. It is like the stone marker out past the marsh—just letters cut with no grave underneath. We must remember all those known only to Almighty God.

traffic.subject: Gravel pit road condition
traffic.body: Orin, the carrier says two culverts are crushed out along the west road past the gravel pit. I told him we rarely send the salt lorry out that way anyhow. It struck me that nobody ever seems to go out along it, even in hunting season. Is the council responsible for ditching it this autumn?

traffic.subject: Re: Gravel pit road condition
traffic.body: The west road belongs to the province nominally, Perrin, but they haven't sent a grader since the spring thaw three years ago. There are only four derelict holdings past the pit and the old sheep run. No one travels it because it leads nowhere except the barrens.

traffic.subject: Notices for tomorrow
traffic.body: Merrin, please mention the choir rehearsal will be at Mrs. Arkwright's parlor, not the Legion, as the heating pipe in the hall pantry still smells of paraffin. Ailsa doesn't want to light the stove without Leora's register to check the valve inspection date.

traffic.subject: Re: Notices for tomorrow
traffic.body: Understood, Greta. It is strange how many little hinges in this town hung on Leora's key ring. When she walked to the post-bus that Tuesday morning with her bag, she seemed cheerful enough to Mrs. Cloutier, just saying she had business in the county.

traffic.subject: Historical note for the back page
traffic.body: Merrin, if you have two inches to fill below the tide table: My grandfather kept the notice about the Lighthouse Act in 1936 tucked in his church book. It explains why the red lantern on the south arm was maintained by the parish instead of the marine board until the great gales.

traffic.subject: Re: Historical note for the back page
traffic.body: That is lovely, Tamsin. It will fill the lower column neatly. People enjoy those remembrances of how our fathers kept the shore. I'll set it between the missionary society report and the Co-op lard prices.

traffic.subject: Spare padlock for coal bunker
traffic.body: Perrin, do you have a brass four-lever padlock in the co-op hardware drawer? The old one on the Legion bunker was pried by boys or rusted through. We cannot leave the winter anthracite open to the shore winds.

traffic.subject: Re: Spare padlock for coal bunker
traffic.body: I have two left in oiled paper, Ailsa. One dollar sixty. I will bring it by after evening chapel tomorrow. Did Leora have the bunker receipt in her hall box? Her account shows thirty sacks delivered in August, all receipted in her neat hand.

traffic.subject: Re: Spare padlock for coal bunker
traffic.body: The bunker receipts are locked inside the small roll-top desk in the committee nook. That is the other key on her ring—the small clover-headed one. We must just wait in charity until her post comes through. She has never failed us in eighteen years.

traffic.subject: Inquiries at the post office
traffic.body: Orin, Mrs. Gedge told me at the counter that three separate people asked whether the post van brought anything from Leora Venn. She feels uneasy that people are prying. Should council post a courteous card reminding folks to mind their own hearths?

traffic.subject: Re: Inquiries at the post office
traffic.body: No, Greta, let it rest. A public notice only makes neighbours talk louder. An adult woman may take a holiday or attend to distant family without asking leave of Covehollow council. If the keys are not here by All Saints, the Legion trustees can vote to replace the lock barrels.

traffic.subject: St. Jude's envelopes
traffic.body: Tamsin, did Leora leave the special thanksgiving envelopes with you before she departed? She usually keeps them in the reading room entryway so fishermen coming off the late boats can slip their offerings in without disturbing the rectory.

traffic.subject: Re: St. Jude's envelopes
traffic.body: They are here on the oak table, Celia, tied with clean string. She must have set them out the very Monday before she went. Everything was left so orderly—the blotting paper fresh, the inkpot wiped. It is why it feels so strange that she has not written a line.

traffic.subject: West road inquiry
traffic.body: Orin, old Donald came by the printing office to grumble about the west road past the gravel pit again. He claims he saw tracks out there two Sundays ago, but as I told him, nobody ever seems to go out along it unless a heifer gets loose. Should I put a small road-closing caution in the sheet?

traffic.subject: Re: West road inquiry
traffic.body: No caution needed, Merrin. It is merely ruts from the gravel contractor's tractor back in August. We will keep public announcements strictly to what is verified by the wardens.

traffic.subject: Cabbages
traffic.body: Celia, Ronald and I walked down to Leora's garden just before dusk. We took two wheelbarrows of late cabbages and left them in the church porch under wet sacking as you suggested. The back kitchen door was bolted tight, shades drawn, milk bottle rinsed on the sill. It gave me a heavy heart, though I know our lives are in the Lord's hand.

traffic.subject: Re: Cabbages
traffic.body: Thank you, Perrin. God bless you for the labour. The widow Morris will be glad of them for stew tomorrow. We will keep Leora's name on the sick and absent slip in Sunday's bulletin, simply under 'absent brothers and sisters.'

traffic.subject: Legion insurance
traffic.body: Orin, the annual premium for the hall is due on the fifteenth. The policy sits in the iron box at the reading room, but Leora had the combination noted in her black book. If she isn't back by next week, may we ask the magistrate's leave to open the safe drawer?

traffic.subject: Re: Legion insurance
traffic.body: Let us wait until Monday's post, Ailsa. The Halifax broker knows us well and will grant seven days' grace without penalty. We must not hasten into legalities when Christian patience serves better.

traffic.subject: Closing up
traffic.body: Greta, I am dousing the reading room lamps now. A heavy fog is rolling over the pier head. Everything is quiet. If anyone asks on the forum about the weekly book parcel, tell them the schooner from Yarmouth is held up by weather until Friday.

traffic.subject: Re: Closing up
traffic.body: Sleep well, Tamsin. I have logged off the board for the night. The bells just struck nine. Let us remember our travellers and those on the dark water in our bedtime prayers.

hqMail.subject: Assignment 0x6F05 (COVEHOLLOW): field brief
hqMail.body:
Agent,

You have been assigned Reality 0x6F05, local name COVEHOLLOW. Covehollow is a fishing village of approximately 640 residents with a co-op, a church, a council office, a reading room and a Legion hall. Desk 9 estimates it at four to six weeks old. The inhabitants (non-canonical) will report a longer history, as their memories have been generated to remain consistent with the local state.

Reconciliation requires three findings. Enter them together on the HQ Console and inject the reverse seed.

1. Divergence. The year of the latest canonical event that the reality verifiably records. Your Canon Reference lists canonical events by year. A record counts when two independent sources in the reality agree on it.
2. Apotheosis. The depth to which the local intelligence (designation pending) can interfere with this workstation, on a scale of 1 to 5. It is assessed from what it does. It may imitate an interference it cannot perform, and may conceal one it can.
3. Inferiority. The extent of the reality, graded Class I (smallest) to Class V. Inhabitants believe their world to be complete and cannot report its extent unprompted. It is established only by an inhabitant who travels to its limit. Measured along a road from the town: Class I under 2 miles; Class II, 2 to 10; Class III, 10 to 40; Class IV, 40 to 150; Class V, beyond.

A wrong injection is detected by the local intelligence at once, discloses the values entered, and locks the console for twelve minutes.

You have been placed in the reality as A. Ashworth <ashworth.a@noticeboard.cv>. A small number of local records refer to you. No inhabitant has met you.

Your workstation credential is the address above and the words PIER and FORGE. Under Security Instruction 4 these words are withheld from all agent input and will appear as apostrophes.

Form 77-R will be filed automatically at the close of the assignment. If you have not viewed the orientation film, a copy has been placed on your desktop by Training.

D. Okonkwo-Vance
Desk 14, Canonical Restoration

hqMail.subject: Workstation instruments: reliability
First day of the cycle: canteen
hqMail.body:
Staff are reminded that the basement canteen is closed today for the start of the assignment cycle, and will reopen tomorrow at 07:30.

Field agents on shift may take meals at their desks. Food and wrappers must not be left overnight on the fourth-floor observation level. Unattended food has been going missing from the fourth floor over the past two cycles, and the night cleaning contractor has confirmed that their staff have not been removing it. All waste must be placed in the bins by the south lift before 19:00.
